name: Terminal fleet wipe through the management plane
summary: An intruder enters through an internet-facing appliance, reaches the network that manages user terminals and disables them in bulk. Modelled on the 2022 KA-SAT attack.

steps.note: Finds a remote-access appliance belonging to the ground network.
Identifies a flaw or misconfiguration in that appliance.
Gains a foothold on the appliance.
Moves into the trusted management segment.
Obtains the ability to issue management commands to terminals.
Uses legitimate management functions, which look routine.
Sends destructive commands to a large share of the fleet.

name: Ground compromise to spacecraft control
summary: A phished operator leads to mission control, command keys and finally unauthorised manoeuvring, with telemetry masked and operators locked out.

steps.note: Identifies operators with command authority.
Compromises an operator workstation through a tailored lure.
Escalates to administrator in the ground environment.
Crosses into mission operations.
Gains use of the command key.
Issues authenticated commands from the control system.
Commands reach the spacecraft over the legitimate uplink.
Telemetry is altered so the ground sees nominal state.
Attitude or orbit control is taken.
Keys are changed to lock the operator out.

name: Rogue uplink against a legacy spacecraft
summary: With public parameters, a recorded downlink and affordable radio equipment, an outsider commands an old spacecraft that lacks link authentication.

steps.note: Recovers frequencies and emissions from filings.
Predicts passes over a site it controls.
Records and characterises the downlink.
Reconstructs command and telemetry formats.
Acquires a transmit-capable station.
Confirms commands are unauthenticated in at least one mode.
Transmits to the spacecraft during a pass.
Injects commands the spacecraft accepts.
Acts while the operator is out of contact.
Forces repeated safe-mode entries.
Uses relaxed protections in safe mode to keep control.

name: Build pipeline to the whole constellation
summary: A compromised dependency survives in the build system, reaches flight through a signed update and is rolled out fleet-wide before it activates.

steps.note: Maps frameworks and suppliers behind the flight software.
Prepares altered code for an upstream project.
The altered dependency is consumed by the build.
Persists in the build and update channel.
Moves from development into operations tooling.
A malicious image is uploaded through the normal process.
Fleet automation applies it to every spacecraft.
The logic stays dormant until a trigger.
Spacecraft are disabled together.
Recovery images were built by the same pipeline.

name: Stolen provider credentials to missed and misused passes
summary: A leaked service key lets an intruder change contact schedules and station configuration at a shared ground provider, and undermine the backup path too.

steps.note: Learns which provider and sites the mission uses.
Finds a provider API key in a public repository.
Signs in to the operator's provider tenant.
Changes schedules and station configuration.
Probes for access to other tenants' resources.
Alters the pass plan fed back to the operator.
The backup path uses the same provider and key.

name: Navigation denial and deception
summary: Local jamming forces receivers to reacquire, then counterfeit signals lead them to a false position or time that dependent systems act on.

steps.note: Identifies users who depend on satellite navigation and timing.
Acquires jamming and signal-generation equipment.
Jams genuine signals in the target area.
Broadcasts counterfeit signals.
Users act on false position or time.

name: Quiet espionage over clear links
summary: Unencrypted traffic on a wide beam yields network details and credentials, which lead to sign-in, data theft and exfiltration hidden in satellite traffic.

steps.note: Surveys unencrypted traffic on the beam.
Collects readable user and backhaul data.
Extracts credentials and internal details from the capture.
Signs in with valid accounts.
Copies design and engineering data.
Moves data out over a satellite link.

name: Earth-observation product deception
summary: Through the customer portal an intruder reaches planning and processing, alters tasking and products, and leaves the operator unable to say which products are sound.

steps.note: Identifies customers who act on the products.
Compromises the customer tasking interface.
Moves into planning and processing systems.
Alters tasking so key areas are not collected.
Modifies delivered products.
Edits logs that would show the changes.
Customers decide on false information.
The operator cannot prove which products are trustworthy.

name: Hosted payload crossover
summary: A third-party payload becomes a position on board, crosses to the platform over the shared bus and shortens the mission through subtle parameter changes.

steps.note: Learns which third parties fly equipment on the platform.
Arrives on board through the hosted payload.
Escalates from the payload domain.
Sends platform messages over the shared bus.
Resides in logic the platform never reads back.
Alters control and power tables slightly.
Consumables are spent early.
The redundant chain shares the same weakness.

name: Extortion of an operator through a supplier account
summary: Bought access leads to data theft, destroyed backups and encrypted mission systems, followed by a return through secrets nobody rotated.

steps.note: Finds supplier credentials in breach data.
Buys a working session from a broker.
Signs in as a valid user.
Escalates to administrator.
Copies engineering and customer data.
Deletes online backups.
Encrypts mission and processing systems.
Demands payment.
Returns later with a token that was never revoked.
